# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: with 100% of traces being uncontrollable INFRA failures (SPA deploy),
  there was no gradient. Chose the framework-endorsed fallback ("robustness gain, don't
  regress"): bounded in-body guards on write tools for policy rules the API leaves
  unchecked. Grounded each in bench_repo/policy.md and validated the derived-value guard
  against the full DB (2000/2000).
- Plateau/stall signal: the true risk this run is that the re-score ALSO infra-errors,
  making every candidate net-zero regardless of quality. If that happens, no edit design
  can move val — it is an environment problem, not a search problem (logged in
  FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md).
- What to try next iteration: only invest in new guards if the re-score produces REAL
  (non-infra) traces with action_check signal. Otherwise the highest-value action is to
  keep the safe bounded guards (they can't regress) rather than spend the last iteration
  on speculative changes.
